title: U.S. House · Florida's 6th District
area: East-central Florida, including Volusia County and parts of Flagler and Lake counties.

context.text: Incumbent Randy Fine defeated Aaron Baker, Daniel Bilzerian and Charles Gambaro in the August 18, 2026 Republican primary. Eric Yonce won the Democratic primary over three opponents. Andrew Parrott (Libertarian), Michael Gist (No Party Affiliation), and Alec Pavlik (write-in, No Party Affiliation) also qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Randy Fine
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary over Aaron Baker, Daniel Bilzerian and Charles Gambaro.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Florida's 6th District (since April 2025)

summary.text: Randy Fine is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 6th District, elected in an April 2025 special election. He previously served in the Florida House and Florida Senate and founded a technology consulting firm.

background.text: Born in Tucson, Arizona; earned a bachelor's degree and an MBA from Harvard University (1996 and 1998).
Founded The Fine Point Group and worked as a technology consultant.
In Congress, serves on the Committee on Education and the Workforce and the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

priorities.text: Support Working Families: says he voted for the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, which he says removes taxes on tips and Social Security and raises the average Floridian's salary by nearly $7,000.
Energy Independence: wants to end U.S. reliance on foreign energy by streamlining permits, reducing regulations, and expanding domestic oil, gas, coal and renewable production.
Eliminate the Department of Education and return control over how children are taught to states, local communities and parents.

positions.summary: Lists standing with President Trump to enforce reciprocal tariffs among his economic priorities.
positions.quote: America First Trade Policy: Stand with President Trump to enforce reciprocal tariffs that keep cheap imports out, bring manufacturing jobs back, and make sure American goods compete on the world stage.

positions.summary: Lists mass deportation of people in the country illegally as one of his top immigration priorities.
positions.quote: Mass Deportations: Nearly 70 million Americans voted for President Trump's plan to remove illegal aliens from our country and restore safety in American communities. Mass deportations mean mass deportations.

positions.summary: Says U.S. energy policy should prioritize ending what he calls "climate extremism" and expanding domestic fossil-fuel and other production rather than pursuing a faster transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: American energy policy must prioritize independence, affordability, and efficiency. That means ending climate extremism, cutting red tape, and putting American producers back in charge of our resources.

positions.summary: Lists empowering law enforcement and backing the use of National Guard and military forces to assist police among his priorities on crime.
positions.quote: Empower Law Enforcement: Despite increased danger from Democrat rhetoric, America's police officers are working harder than ever and volunteering at higher rates because of the Trump effect. I stand with them and will always have their back.

positions.summary: Says families, not the federal government, should choose among public, private, charter or homeschool options for their children.
positions.quote: Champion School Choice: Families, not Washington, should decide the best path for their children, whether public, private, charter, or homeschool. Competition improves outcomes and ensures every child has a chance to succeed.

positions.summary: Says he fully supports the U.S. alliance with Israel against Hamas and other adversaries.
positions.quote: Stand with Israel: As a proud Jewish American, I fully support our alliance with Israel in the fight against Hamas, Al Qaeda, and all enemies of Western civilization.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities above are drawn from Fine's official House issues pages (Economy, Immigration, Crime, Education, Energy, Foreign Policy). Federal roll-call votes, sponsored-bill lists and FEC finance totals for this sitting member are added by script.

candidates.name: Eric Yonce
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over three opponents.

summary.text: Eric Yonce is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 6th Congressional District. Born and raised in the district, he spent over 20 years in retail management before entering real estate and starting a small business remodeling vintage Airstream trailers.

background.text: Grew up in Florida's 6th District; his mother led the local Realtor Association and his father is a retired police officer.
Spent more than 20 years in big-box retail management.
Completed a 2,000+ mile thru-hike of the Appalachian Trail in 2022, then entered real estate and started a small business remodeling vintage Airstream trailers.

priorities.text: Says he is not a career politician and wants to bring true representation to the district.
Opposes overdevelopment that strains resources, threatens the environment and increases flood risk; supports smart-growth policies.
Wants to address the rising cost of housing, energy and everyday expenses.

positions.summary: Says the district faces unprecedented overdevelopment that strains resources and threatens the environment, and calls for smart-growth policies rather than continued rapid building.

candidates.name: Michael Gist
candidates.ballotNote: Unofficially withdrew from the race but remains on the November 3 general-election ballot.

summary.text: Michael Gist is a no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 6th Congressional District. He is a 14-year Marine Corps veteran and former public-school teacher from Volusia County running on a proposal he calls 'Freedom Accounts.'

background.text: Served 14 years in the U.S. Marine Corps and later taught in Volusia County public schools.
Describes his family as lifelong residents of Volusia County for over 100 years.

priorities.text: Proposes 'Freedom Accounts,' a market-based plan redirecting government spending into personal investment accounts for education, homeownership, healthcare and long-term security.
Says he is running as an independent because he believes both major parties are dominated by elites rather than ordinary people.
